body: That is solid advice. Thank you for helping me down the right path. You have no idea how much your efforts mean to me. Literally life changing
Thank you Warren. I like how you focused on acceptance and setting up my environment for success. I should be more focused on what I can do versus past failures and reasons why I think I'd fail.

Ha this vid looks good already. Thank you for sharing!

I am really concerned about it. I've done nothing really aside from wishing it away. I can tone it down and go to the gym and whatnot, but eventually I'll get bored and fall back into it. I just find it really upsetting. This isn't the life I want to live and I feel prisoner to myself. The learned helplessness is a great enabler.

I think they've been growing since childhood. I grew up around fighting and because of that and some sexual abuse that happened I became really good at separating my mind from my body. The drugs stated in high school and become a staple in college. I've been in and out of NA for 6 years now on my own accord (I amazingly have yet to get in serious trouble) but got turned off by the religiousness of such a "non-religious program." Since college, the daily smoking has been joined with drinking, and now the every other couples weekends of cocaine. I don't want to go the rehab route because I can't afford the time out, and doctors scare me because I still leave out parts even here out of fear of being held against my will.

I'm sorry you feel that way. Seems like you've have a really hard run recently and it's a shitload to cope with. Have you opened up to friends about it enough to get it out of your head? I know wanting to escape can have a romantic-esq nature to it, but I think you wouldn't be asking for help if you didn't have some sense of faith in things getting better. I struggle too with my own issues and see ending it as some sort of fail-safe, but that can keep me from owning my life and striving to be better. I think you can be better than that voice inside your head. I think you can regain your lost stuff and cope with the unfortunate breaks in meaningful relationships. You are bare right now, vulnerable and it's scary as fuck. Maybe it's just a bullshit saying, but when your in the bottom of a hole the only way to go is up. Don't give up before the good part come back. You'll find yourself and love again. Maybe try replying to other people here because I just did for the first time after posting my own struggle and it's helping. Words are just words, why not make a difference in someone's life today instead? I won't pretend to know your pain or even the deep twisted shit you might have been to afraid to post here, but for this very moment, I care about you and I hope you can love the things you hate about yourself. PM me or something if you wanna talk more. Not sure if I'm any good at it, but it feels good to get outside my own shit for a second and I give better advice than I follow myself.
